title: Personal suggestions a shopper can actually get
summary: What a shopper does becomes a short description of their taste, which finds similar items that are in stock, in their size and nearby, with a virtual fitting room at the end.

nodes.label: Similar
nodes.caption: items like the ones you love

nodes.label: You can get
nodes.caption: in stock, your size, near you

nodes.label: Try it on
nodes.caption: on your photo, after a size

steps.title: Signals
steps.caption: Viewed 12 items today, stayed 40 s on linen dresses, saved 3 favorites, bought size M last month, near the Vila Nova store.
steps.engineering: Client events with consent; dwell time and saves weighted higher than views.
steps.presenterNote: Every signal is something the shopper already did: what they looked at, lingered on, saved and bought, and which store is close.

steps.title: Your taste
steps.caption: linen · neutral tones · midi · size M. A short description of your taste that anyone could read out loud.
steps.engineering: A per-user profile built from recent product embeddings, weighted by signal strength and recency.
steps.presenterNote: From that we build a short description of their taste that you could read out loud: linen, neutral tones, midi, size M.

steps.title: Only what you can get
steps.caption: Similar items that are in stock, in your size, near you. Nothing you would fall for and then fail to buy.
steps.engineering: Vector similarity, then re-ranked by stock-in-size, pickup distance and margin; business rules are versioned.
steps.presenterNote: Here's the product point: a suggestion that's out of stock or not in your size feels smart and sells nothing, so we only show what they can actually get.

steps.title: Try it on
steps.caption: See it on your photo before buying. It opens once you pick a size, so every try is a serious one.
steps.engineering: A third-party try-on service, opened only after a size is chosen, to control cost per try.
steps.presenterNote: Finally a virtual fitting room, which we buy rather than build, and only open once a size is chosen, because every try costs money.
